analysis:
The PR changes only CI review tooling under .github/scripts/threat_review: Bedrock call budgeting (bedrock.py), the run lifecycle and report text (budget_runner.py), and the scanner's call planning (budget_scan.py). It changes no provider runtime, coordinator, attestation, key or cache-storage code, so none of the canonical threat IDs (T-041, TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-009, TB-011, A-xxx) are directly affected. I identified no regression against the threat model.

Security-relevant behavior I examined:
- bedrock.py 46-83: a new 'workload' call policy. plan_calls() raises BudgetStopped when the planned calls plus 1 exceed BEDROCK_SCAN_MAX_WORKLOAD_CALLS (hard-capped at 100 by bounded()). limit starts at 0 in workload mode, so any call without a prior plan hits BEDROCK_CALL_LIMIT. This fails closed.
- Fallback to OpenRouter remains restricted to explicit UNAVAILABLE codes (bedrock.py 23-24, 172-173). Uncertain failures do not resample.
- Accounting failure still stops later calls (bedrock.py 87, 113-119).
- budget_runner.py 175-177: reruns with GITHUB_RUN_ATTEMPT other than 1 are refused inside the try block, so the exception path sets finished=True and the report says human review is required. Because the check precedes the THREAT_REVIEW_ENABLED check, a rerun cannot spend paid calls. This limits cost-abuse attack surface.
- budget_runner.py 38-48: the report now says 'Human review required' when incomplete and finished or errors exist, and 'Scan completed.' otherwise. The final 'Scan completed.' branch requires complete (integration done, full coverage, no errors, no pending depth), so it does not falsely signal clearance. The clearance gate itself (THREAT_REVIEW_REQUIRE_CLEARANCE and the result file) is unchanged and still depends on snapshot content.
- budget_scan.py: plan_calls is called before the source, depth and integration batches. Integration rounds are planned per round, so the ceiling stops non-converging loops. The planner is called with getattr, so the OpenRouter path is unaffected. The finished flag is set after the try/except in run(), after errors are recorded. In the lifecycle exception path it is set explicitly.

Remaining questions (outside the supplied evidence): the CI workflow file and its removal of paid dispatch are not shown. I did not review how the workflow sets BEDROCK_SCAN_CALL_POLICY or how the clearance consumer treats the new 'finished' field. Neither affects the provider threat model directly.
